summary: Brian's macro setup: a Strait of Hormuz disruption would choke helium (30-38% of global supply from Qatar, used to cool fiber lasers and seal high-capacity hard drives), LNG and the sulfur used to etch chip wafers — and he screens for ten tech names passing his filter of two-quarter margin expansion, named hyperscaler contracts and production booked through 2027. Storage and optical: Lumentum (LITE, CONDITIONAL_BUY), the dominant 200G-per-lane EML laser supplier facing a projected 36% 2026 supply shortfall, backed by Nvidia's $2B investment; Ciena (CIEN, BUY), the coherent-optics leader with revenue up 40% and full-year guidance raised to $6.3B, bought on the post-earnings pullback; Seagate (STX, CONDITIONAL_BUY), whose helium-sealed HAMR drives let it raise prices 20-30% with contracts through fiscal 2027; Western Digital (WDC, CONDITIONAL_BUY), the cleaner-balance-sheet version of the Seagate trade with its first-ever 50%+ gross margin; Credo (CRDO, CONDITIONAL_BUY), whose copper cables bypass the laser supply chain entirely as hyperscalers redesign racks, revenue tripled; Astera Labs (ALAB, CONDITIONAL_BUY), retimers and fabric switches for those rack redesigns, 93% growth at 76% margin. Power: Constellation (CEG, CONDITIONAL_BUY), the largest US nuclear fleet plus the Calpine deal, capturing gas-price spillover; Talen (TLN, CONDITIONAL_BUY), the $18B Amazon Susquehanna contract; Bloom Energy (BE, CONDITIONAL_BUY), fuel cells shipping in months with Oracle, AEP and Brookfield deals; Powell Industries (POWL, CONDITIONAL_BUY), switchgear with backlog rising $1.8B to $2.2B. High conviction in the businesses, discipline on entries — don't chase at all-time highs. A Seeking Alpha sponsorship segment is included.
title: History Is Being Made. You Only Get One Chance!
